steps.text: Combine brown sugar, black pepper, onion powder, paprika, and salt in a bowl; rub onto pork chops until coated. Cover chops; refrigerate 6 hours to overnight.
Set an oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source and preheat the oven's broiler.
Place pork chops on a slotted, two-piece broiler pan. Whisk maple syrup and mustard together in a small bowl; set aside.

Broil pork chops in the preheated oven for 5 minutes; flip chops. Broil 5 minutes more. Brush chops with maple syrup glaze; broil 1 minute. Flip chops; brush with glaze. Broil until cooked to your desired degree of doneness, about 1 minute. Transfer chops to serving plates; top with additional glaze, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Maple-Mustard Glazed Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: This boneless maple-mustard pork chops recipe starts with a dry rub before broiling, then brushing with a maple mustard glaze. Tangy, sweet, spicy!

review.reviewBody:
I was limited on time so I modified this recipe a bit. I rubbed the pork chops in the dry ingredients, and placed them on a flat griddle. I mixed the mustard and real syrup and poured spoonfuls over the top.

I turned the pork chops after about 8 minutes and poured more of the glaze on.

I did reduce the pepper to a single teaspoon but I think next time I'll only use a 1/4 of a teaspoon. And maybe get a spicer brown mustard. 

Overall great flavors, easy dinner.

Very Good! I made many changes because of lack of time and ingredients. I used onion soup mix because I had no onion powder. I reduced the amount of salt because of the salt already in the soup mix. I used dijon mustard. I used pancake syrup insead of maple syrup. I mixed all of the ingredients together (I didn't have time to marinate). Put some olive oil in a frying pan (med-high heat). I seared the chops on both sides and then added the mixture to the pan, covered it and simmered the sauce and chops about 15 min. It was great!!!!!! My husband loved it. Will definitely make this again....probably the same way because I didn't have to plan ahead.

This turned out really well for me! I felt like that tablespoon of pepper sounded like an awful lot, so I reduced it to a half tablespoon, and added a half teaspoon of crushed red pepper. I also reduced the brown sugar to heaping 1/8 cup, and that worked well for my household. I marinated for about 7 hours. Following another reviewer, I also seared my two very thick pork steaks over medium high heat (in my cast iron skillet), poured the glaze over, and then simmered until done. It took longer this way, but I kept an eye on it and it didn't over cook, turning out tender and juicy. I reduced the glaze in the skillet while the steaks rested, and that glaze really made the dish perfect, with that spicy sweet flavor. Yum! Only four stars because I did make changes, but when I make this again, I'll cook in the same fashion. Thanks for the recipe!

My family really liked this. I used part maple syrup and part table syrup, and less pepper. I didn't have time to marinate long, only had it sit for about 30 minutes. I pan fried the chops and they were awesome. I am going to try adding some cayenne next time to give it a little more spice to counteract the sweet. Will definitely make this again!

Simple recipe with great flavor. I did it a little differently with the same ingredients. I rubbed the dry seasoning onto both sides of the chops which I had placed on a foil-lined cookie sheet. Next I spooned the Dijon mustard over them and sprinkled with brown sugar. Refrigerated for a couple of hrs, then drizzled maple syrup over them and baked for 30 min at 350. I drained and reserved the juices, flipped them over and added a little more syrup on each side then broiled on high for abt 2 min per side. (Mine were 1/2” thin boneless chops, so easily overcooked). After removing from oven, I poured a bit of the leftover juices on each chop and let them stand for a few minutes. Served with mashed potatoes and sliced carrots, this meal was delicious! The chops were very tender and full of flavor! Will definitely make these often! Thanks for this recipe, even tho my method was different, the flavors were on point! And just as an FYI, the mustard, which my hubby hates, is really just for tenderizing the meat…he nor I could taste it. Easy and yummy!

Wasn't paying close attention and mixed all ingredients including syrup together at once and marinated 30 minutes before I realized it. Broiled about 4 min per side then put chops and sauce in baking dish covered in foil and baked 350 for 30 minutes. It was excellent! I also used smoked paprika for a little heat. Spicy and sweet is my favorite and I will up this sauce for many other things.

I've prepared this twice in the last 2 weeks and it will be in regular rotation for me, ongoing. I used boneless pork chops the first time and a 1lb pork tenderloin the second time, both successfully. I did modify the recipe a bit, and used steak & chop grill seasoning I got from Aldi instead of the salt, pepper, onion powder and paprika. So, I combined the 1/4 cup of brown sugar and a tablespoon of the grill seasoning for the dry rub. I only marinated the meat for a couple hours each time and then followed the rest of the recipe. Super delicious!

This is the best pork chop recipe I have tried in a long time! But....I didn't find it until 30 minutes before cooking dinner, so I made a small change. Since I didn't have time to marinate, I rubbed the pork chops with olive oil, then applied the rub. Put in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. Then, instead of broiling, I placed them on the grill and grilled them. I grilled them at 375 degrees, 5 minutes on each side, then 1 minute with the glaze, turned them over, and 1 more minute with the glaze. They were awesome and my husband said he could eat them every night!!!!

Thanks so much for the recipe!

I will definitely make this again! The picture is exactly how I served it-absolutely delicious. I sautéed some fresh spinach in olive oil and kosher salt and added a little of the mustard-maple glaze. Put the spinach on the bottom, mash potatoes on top of the spinach, and the pork chop on top. Love the savory-sweetness of it all! The only mistake I made was using pure ground pepper instead of freshly ground (Way too much pepper because I used the full Tablespoon of finely ground pure pepper!) Thanks for sharing!

This was great! Only thing I did was add a little chili powder to the rub because other reviews said it needed a little cayenne or something. It's hot here right now so I didn't want to turn on the broiler. I pan seared the pork and added the sauce, turned it to low for five minutes. My husband has said three different times how good it was even though he doesn't really like sweet sauces. This was a hit with the whole family and I'll definitely make it again!

Wow, these are REALLY good. I used thin cut pork chops, marinated them overnight and then just cooked them on the stove top since I hate broiling. They turned out so good! They are a tad sweet though so I might cut back on the brown sugar a bit next time.
This one was a lot of fun.. I never thought to mix Mustard and maple syrup to make a glaze we'll definitely be making this again

I didn't have time to let the pork chops set, so I put them on a hot, oiled griddle right after coating them with the dry rub. Cooked them 7-8 minutes on each side; then brushed on the glaze. After frying them for 1 minute, I flipped them over, glazed again & fried for 1 more minute. They were good this way too! 😋👍
This recipe was so easy and absolutely delicious! I’ve tried several pork chop recipes and none have had this much flavor. Loved the spicy coating and sauce. It really brought the pork chops to life!
This was very tasty, will be making the again.
My boys loved the recipe. Suggest doubling up on the marinade for a gravy sauce on the potatos.

Awesome recipe! Easy and delicious. Followed the recipe with absolutely no changes, pork was tender and juicy. The rub and the glaze are wonderful.

Thank you for sharing!
very good although the loin chops I used were too thin to cook long enough to get a good crust.
Easy to follow directions, tasted great
I made this tonight but we barbequed it. It was amazing, so much flavor. Husband asked for it to go on the rotation.
